claim: Human CARD8 senses HIV-1 infection via site-specific cleavage of the CARD8 N-terminus by HIV-1 protease (HIV-1PR).
source: Here, we find that the human inflammasome-forming sensor CARD8 senses HIV-1 infection via site-specific cleavage of the CARD8 N-terminus by the HIV protease (HIV-1 PR ).
evidence: The manuscript presents experimental data showing HIV-1PR cleavage of CARD8 in multiple assays (Figures 1, 3, 4, 5) and functional inflammasome activation upon HIV-1 infection.

claim: HIV-1PR cleavage of CARD8 induces pyroptotic cell death from infected cells.
source: HIV-1 PR cleavage of CARD8 induces pyroptotic cell death and the release of pro-inflammatory cytokines from infected cells
evidence: The manuscript presents data showing increased cell death measured by PI uptake in HIV-1 infected cells in a CARD8-dependent manner (Figure 3).

claim: HIV-1PR cleavage of CARD8 induces release of pro-inflammatory cytokines from infected cells.
source: HIV-1 PR cleavage of CARD8 induces pyroptotic cell death and the release of pro-inflammatory cytokines from infected cells
evidence: The manuscript presents data showing IL-1β secretion after HIV-1 infection in a CARD8-dependent manner (Figures 3, 4, 5).

claim: Pyroptotic cell death and cytokine release processes are regulated by Toll-like receptor stimulation prior to viral infection.
source: HIV-1 PR cleavage of CARD8 induces pyroptotic cell death and the release of pro-inflammatory cytokines from infected cells, processes regulated by Toll-like receptor stimulation prior to viral infection.
evidence: The manuscript shows that TLR priming is required for IL-1β secretion and enhances cell death after HIV-1 infection (Figure 3B).

claim: In acutely infected cells, CARD8 senses the activity of de novo translated HIV-1PR.
source: In acutely infected cells, CARD8 senses the activity of both de novo translated HIV-1 PR and packaged HIV-1 PR that is released from the incoming virion.
evidence: The manuscript shows CARD8-dependent inflammasome activation at 24 hours post-infection, a timepoint consistent with de novo viral protein synthesis (Figure 4A).

claim: In acutely infected cells, CARD8 senses the activity of packaged HIV-1PR that is released from the incoming virion.
source: In acutely infected cells, CARD8 senses the activity of both de novo translated HIV-1 PR and packaged HIV-1 PR that is released from the incoming virion.
evidence: The manuscript shows CARD8-dependent inflammasome activation as early as 2 hours post-infection, prior to reverse transcription and de novo viral protein synthesis (Figure 4A).

claim: The HIV-1PR cleavage site in human CARD8 arose after the divergence of chimpanzees and humans.
source: Moreover, our evolutionary analyses reveal that the HIV-1 PR cleavage site in human CARD8 arose after the divergence of chimpanzees and humans.
evidence: The manuscript presents phylogenetic alignment showing that only human CARD8 has phenylalanine at position 60 (F60), which is required for HIV-1PR cleavage, while chimpanzee CARD8 has leucine at this position (Figure 1A).

claim: Chimpanzee CARD8 does not recognize proteases from HIV.
source: Although chimpanzee CARD8 does not recognize proteases from HIV or simian immunodeficiency viruses from chimpanzees (SIVcpz)
evidence: The manuscript shows that chimpanzee CARD8 is not cleaved by HIV-1PR in cleavage assays (Figure 2A) and does not restore inflammasome activation in complementation assays (Figure 5D-F).

claim: Chimpanzee CARD8 does not recognize proteases from simian immunodeficiency viruses from chimpanzees (SIVcpz).
source: Although chimpanzee CARD8 does not recognize proteases from HIV or simian immunodeficiency viruses from chimpanzees (SIVcpz)
evidence: The manuscript shows that chimpanzee CARD8 is not cleaved by SIVcpzPR in cleavage assays (Figure 2A).

claim: SIVcpz cleaves human CARD8.
source: SIVcpz does cleave human CARD8
evidence: The manuscript shows that both SIVcpzEK505 and SIVcpzLB7 proteases cleave human CARD8 in cleavage assays (Figure 2A).

claim: SIVcpz was poised to activate the human CARD8 inflammasome prior to its cross-species transmission into humans.
source: suggesting that SIVcpz was poised to activate the human CARD8 inflammasome prior to its cross-species transmission into humans.
evidence: The manuscript shows that SIVcpzPR cleaves human CARD8 but not chimpanzee CARD8, and that the F59-F60 motif in human CARD8 arose before HIV-1 emergence (Figures 1A, 2A).

claim: The HIV-1 protease (HIV-1PR) cleaves human CARD8 between phenylalanine 59 (P1) and F60 (P1').
source: The HIV-1 protease (HIV-1PR) cleaves human CARD8 between phenylalanine (F) 59 (P1) and F60 (P1') (Figure 1A; Wang et al., 2021).
evidence: The manuscript cites prior work (Wang et al., 2021) and presents phylogenetic alignment showing the cleavage site (Figure 1A).

claim: The amino acid P1 site, F59, is invariant among hominoids, gibbons, and Old World monkeys.
source: While the amino acid P1 site, F59, is invariant among hominoids, gibbons, and Old World monkeys
evidence: The manuscript presents phylogenetic alignment showing F59 conservation across these primate species (Figure 1A).

claim: Only human CARD8 has a phenylalanine at the P1' site, F60.
source: only human CARD8 has a phenylalanine at the P1' site, F60 (Figure 1A).
evidence: The manuscript presents phylogenetic alignment showing that only human CARD8 has F60, while other primates have different amino acids at this position (Figure 1A).

claim: The F59-F60 motif arose in the human lineage after the most recent common ancestor with chimpanzees and bonobos.
source: The F59-F60 motif therefore must have arisen in the human lineage after the most recent common ancestor with chimpanzees and bonobos.
evidence: The manuscript shows that chimpanzee and bonobo CARD8 have leucine at position 60, while human CARD8 has phenylalanine (Figure 1A).

claim: The F59-F60 motif is present in Homo neanderthalensis (Neanderthal) CARD8.
source: The F59-F60 motif is also present in Homo neanderthalensis (i.e. Neanderthal) CARD8 (Figure 1A)
evidence: The manuscript presents phylogenetic alignment showing F59-F60 in Neanderthal CARD8 (Figure 1A).

claim: The F59-F60 motif emergence can be conservatively dated within the last million years.
source: conservatively dating its emergence within the last million years (Green et al., 2010).
evidence: The manuscript cites Green et al., 2010 regarding the timing of human-Neanderthal divergence.

claim: Wildtype human CARD8 is cleaved upon transfection of HIV-1 and HIV-2 proviruses.
source: Indeed, we found that wildtype (WT) human CARD8 with an N-terminal mCherry fusion is cleaved upon transfection of HIV-1 and HIV-2 proviruses, resulting in an ~33 kDa product (Figure 1B and C, top blot).
evidence: The manuscript presents immunoblot data showing CARD8 cleavage products after co-transfection with HIV proviruses (Figure 1C).

claim: The HIVPR inhibitor lopinavir blocks both Gag processing and CARD8 cleavage.
source: Cleavage of CARD8 in these experiments was dependent on the protease encoded by the Gag-Pol gene of these proviruses as the HIVPR inhibitor lopinavir (LPV) blocked both Gag processing of p55gag to p41gag and p24gag and CARD8 cleavage (Figure 1C, top and middle blot).
evidence: The manuscript presents immunoblot data showing that lopinavir treatment prevents CARD8 cleavage and Gag processing (Figure 1C).

claim: HIVPR cleavage of WT human CARD8 (F60) is much more efficient than cleavage of human CARD8 F60L or F60S.
source: HIVPR cleavage of WT human CARD8 (F60) was much more efficient than cleavage of human CARD8 F60L or F60S (Figure 1D)
evidence: The manuscript presents immunoblot data comparing cleavage efficiency of WT and mutant CARD8 (Figure 1D).

claim: Species-specific variation at position 60 impacts CARD8 recognition of HIVPR activity.
source: These results indicate that species-specific variation at position 60 impacts CARD8 recognition of HIVPR activity.
evidence: The manuscript shows differential cleavage efficiency of CARD8 variants with different amino acids at position 60 (Figure 1D).

claim: Both SIVcpzEK505 and SIVcpzLB7 proteases cleave human CARD8.
source: Like HIV-1 and HIV-2 proteases, we found that both SIVcpz proteases (SIVcpzPR) cleaved human CARD8 (Figure 2A)
evidence: The manuscript presents immunoblot data showing cleavage of human CARD8 by SIVcpz proteases (Figure 2A).

claim: SIVcpzPR had a pre-existing ability to cleave human CARD8 prior to spillover.
source: suggesting that SIVcpzPR had a pre-existing ability to cleave human CARD8 prior to spillover.
evidence: The manuscript shows that SIVcpz proteases cleave human CARD8, and the F59-F60 motif arose before HIV-1 emergence (Figures 1A, 2A).

claim: SIVcpzPR does not cleave chimpanzee CARD8.
source: To deduce whether or not this cleavage is unique to humans, we also tested SIVcpzPR ability to cleave chimpanzee CARD8 (Figure 2A) and F60L and F60S human CARD8 variants (Figure 2B) and found that none of the other CARD8 variants could be cleaved by SIVcpzPR.
evidence: The manuscript presents immunoblot data showing lack of cleavage of chimpanzee CARD8 by SIVcpzPR (Figure 2A).

claim: SIVcpzPR does not cleave F60L and F60S human CARD8 variants.
source: we also tested SIVcpzPR ability to cleave chimpanzee CARD8 (Figure 2A) and F60L and F60S human CARD8 variants (Figure 2B) and found that none of the other CARD8 variants could be cleaved by SIVcpzPR.
evidence: The manuscript presents immunoblot data showing lack of cleavage of F60L and F60S CARD8 variants by SIVcpzPR (Figure 2B).

claim: SIVmac239PR cleaves WT human CARD8.
source: Moreover, SIVmac239PR also cleaved WT human CARD8, an event that was greatly reduced when tested against the human CARD8 cleavage mutant F60A (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The manuscript presents immunoblot data showing cleavage of WT human CARD8 by SIVmac239PR (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).

claim: SIVmac239PR cleavage of human CARD8 is greatly reduced for the F60A mutant.
source: Moreover, SIVmac239PR also cleaved WT human CARD8, an event that was greatly reduced when tested against the human CARD8 cleavage mutant F60A (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The manuscript presents immunoblot data comparing cleavage of WT and F60A CARD8 by SIVmac239PR (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).

claim: The F59-F60 motif renders human CARD8 uniquely susceptible to cleavage by a broad range of primate lentiviral proteases.
source: Moreover, the F59-F60 motif that arose in the human lineage renders human CARD8 uniquely susceptible to cleavage at that position by a broad range of primate lentiviral proteases.
evidence: The manuscript shows that HIV-1, HIV-2, SIVcpz, and SIVmac proteases all cleave human CARD8 but not other primate CARD8 variants (Figures 1, 2).

claim: Some HIV-1PR is active in the cytoplasm.
source: However, we observed Gag processing of p55gag to p41gag and p24gag in cytoplasmic lysates of THP-1 cells infected with either WT HIV-1LAI or HIV-1LAI that was pseudotyped with the vesicular stomatitis virus glycoprotein (VSV-g) instead of its own envelope (HIV-1LAI-VSVG), consistent with prior studies demonstrating that some HIV-1PR is active in the cytoplasm (Figure 3A; Alvarez et al., 2006; Tabler et al., 2022).
evidence: The manuscript presents immunoblot data showing Gag processing in cytoplasmic lysates and cites prior studies (Alvarez et al., 2006; Tabler et al., 2022) (Figure 3A).

claim: HIV-1 infection induces cell death in THP-1 cells as measured by propidium iodide uptake.
source: For both HIV-1-infected and VbP-treated THP-1 cells, we observed an increase in cell death compared to mock-infected controls as measured by uptake of the membrane-impermeable dye propidium iodide (PI) (Figure 3B, left).
evidence: The manuscript presents flow cytometry data showing increased PI uptake in HIV-1 infected cells (Figure 3B, left).

claim: VbP treatment induces cell death in THP-1 cells as measured by propidium iodide uptake.
source: For both HIV-1-infected and VbP-treated THP-1 cells, we observed an increase in cell death compared to mock-infected controls as measured by uptake of the membrane-impermeable dye propidium iodide (PI) (Figure 3B, left).
evidence: The manuscript presents flow cytometry data showing increased PI uptake in VbP-treated cells (Figure 3B, left).

claim: Neither HIV-1 infection nor VbP alone leads to an increase in IL-1β levels without priming.
source: However, neither HIV-1 infection nor VbP alone led to an increase in IL-1β levels (Figure 3B, right, no prime condition)
evidence: The manuscript presents IL-1β secretion data showing no increase without TLR priming (Figure 3B, right).

claim: VbP treatment and HIV-1LAI-VSVG infection induce cell death independent of priming.
source: We found that VbP treatment and HIV-1LAI-VSVG infection induce cell death independent of priming, although TLR agonists did elevate cell death responses in some instances (Figure 3B left).
evidence: The manuscript presents cell death data showing responses in both primed and unprimed conditions (Figure 3B, left).

claim: The release of IL-1β after HIV-1 infection or VbP treatment is entirely dependent on TLR priming.
source: In contrast, the release of IL-1β after HIV-1 infection or VbP treatment was entirely dependent on TLR priming (Figure 3B, right).
evidence: The manuscript presents IL-1β secretion data showing responses only in primed conditions (Figure 3B, right).

claim: HIV-1 infection alone is sufficient to induce cell death in THP-1 cells.
source: Thus, HIV-1 infection alone (i.e. in the absence of molecules causing premature dimerization of Gag-Pol) is sufficient to induce cell death in THP-1 cells
evidence: The manuscript shows cell death in HIV-1 infected cells without NNRTI treatment (Figure 3B).

claim: Priming via TLR stimulation is required for HIV-1 infection-induced IL-1β secretion.
source: and priming (e.g. via TLR stimulation) is required for HIV-1 infection-induced IL-1β secretion and elevated levels of cell death.
evidence: The manuscript shows IL-1β secretion only occurs in primed cells after HIV-1 infection (Figure 3B).

claim: IL-1β secretion, cell death, and CASP1 activation are significantly reduced in CARD8 KO versus WT THP-1 cells following HIV-1 infection.
source: Similar to our observations with VbP, we found that IL-1β secretion, cell death, and CASP1 activation (as measured by FLICA assay) were significantly reduced in CARD8 KO versus WT THP-1 cells following HIV-1 infection (Figure 3B).
evidence: The manuscript presents data comparing WT and CARD8 KO cells showing reduced responses in KO cells (Figure 3B).

claim: The inflammasome response to HIV-1 infection in THP-1 cells is primarily dependent on CARD8.
source: Because responses to HIV-1 infection were reduced to a similar level in both CARD8 KO cells and CASP1 KO cells, our findings suggest that the inflammasome response to HIV-1 infection in THP-1 cells is primarily dependent on CARD8
evidence: The manuscript shows similar reduction in responses in both CARD8 KO and CASP1 KO cells (Figure 3B).

claim: The inflammasome response to HIV-1 infection in THP-1 cells is independent of HIV-1 envelope.
source: our findings suggest that the inflammasome response to HIV-1 infection in THP-1 cells is primarily dependent on CARD8, but independent of HIV-1 envelope.
evidence: The manuscript shows similar responses to both WT HIV-1LAI and VSV-g pseudotyped HIV-1LAI (Figure 3B).

claim: HIV-1Q23-BG505 infection results in IL-1β secretion in a CARD8-dependent manner.
source: HIV-1Q23-BG505 infection also resulted in IL-1β secretion in a CARD8-dependent manner, suggesting that CARD8-dependent inflammasome activation is conserved across HIV-1 strains.
evidence: The manuscript presents data showing IL-1β secretion in WT but not CARD8 KO cells after HIV-1Q23-BG505 infection (Figure 3D).

claim: CARD8-dependent inflammasome activation is conserved across HIV-1 strains.
source: suggesting that CARD8-dependent inflammasome activation is conserved across HIV-1 strains.
evidence: The manuscript shows CARD8-dependent responses to multiple HIV-1 strains (HIV-1LAI, HIV-1Q23-BG505) (Figures 3B, 3D).

claim: There is a statistically significant, CARD8-dependent increase in IL-1β as early as 2 hr after HIV-1 infection.
source: Unexpectedly, we revealed a statistically significant, CARD8-dependent increase in IL-1β as early as 2 hr after infection (the first timepoint assayed after the initial infection), which plateaued for the next 6 hr and then further increased by 24 hr post-infection (Figure 4A).
evidence: The manuscript presents time-course data showing IL-1β secretion at 2 hours post-infection (Figure 4A).

claim: CARD8-dependent IL-1β increase plateaus for 6 hours after the initial 2-hour increase, then further increases by 24 hr post-infection.
source: we revealed a statistically significant, CARD8-dependent increase in IL-1β as early as 2 hr after infection (the first timepoint assayed after the initial infection), which plateaued for the next 6 hr and then further increased by 24 hr post-infection (Figure 4A).
evidence: The manuscript presents time-course data showing IL-1β levels over time (Figure 4A).

claim: The early timepoints of CARD8 activation (2 hr) are sampled prior to reverse-transcription and the genesis of de novo synthesized HIV-1 transcripts.
source: As the early timepoints were sampled prior to reverse-transcription and the genesis of de novo synthesized HIV-1 transcripts (Mohammadi et al., 2013)
evidence: The manuscript cites Mohammadi et al., 2013 regarding the timing of reverse transcription and compares to the 2-hour timepoint.

claim: CARD8 detects the activity of packaged HIV-1PR released into the target cell upon viral entry.
source: these findings raised the possibility that CARD8 detects the activity of packaged HIV-1PR released into the target cell upon viral entry as well as de novo synthesized Gag-Pol.
evidence: The manuscript shows CARD8 activation at 2 hours post-infection, before de novo viral protein synthesis (Figure 4A).

claim: The HIVPR inhibitor lopinavir blocks CARD8 inflammasome activation by HIV-1 infection.
source: To test this hypothesis, we treated target cells with the HIVPR inhibitor LPV, which blocked CARD8 inflammasome activation by HIV-1 infection, reinforcing that CARD8 senses HIV-1PR activity.
evidence: The manuscript presents data showing that lopinavir treatment prevents IL-1β secretion after HIV-1 infection (Figure 4B).

claim: An HIV-1 virus lacking Vpr (ΔVpr) induces CARD8-dependent inflammasome activation.
source: However, we found that an HIV-1 virus lacking Vpr (ΔVpr) also induces CARD8-dependent inflammasome activation (Figure 4B).
evidence: The manuscript presents data showing IL-1β secretion after infection with HIV-1 ΔVpr (Figure 4B).

claim: HIV-1 infection induces inflammasome activation upon CARD8 detection of HIV-1PR released from the incoming virion.
source: Thus, our findings suggest that HIV-1 infection induces inflammasome activation upon CARD8 detection of HIV-1PR released from the incoming virion as well as newly translated HIV-1PR.
evidence: The manuscript shows CARD8 activation at early timepoints (2 hr) before de novo viral protein synthesis (Figure 4A).

claim: HIV-1 infection induces inflammasome activation upon CARD8 detection of newly translated HIV-1PR.
source: Thus, our findings suggest that HIV-1 infection induces inflammasome activation upon CARD8 detection of HIV-1PR released from the incoming virion as well as newly translated HIV-1PR.
evidence: The manuscript shows continued increase in CARD8 activation at later timepoints (24 hr) consistent with de novo viral protein synthesis (Figure 4A).

claim: CARD8 KO THP-1 cells complemented with WT CARD8 undergo IL-1β secretion and cell death in response to VbP in a dox-dependent manner.
source: We found that CARD8 KO THP-1 cells complemented with WT CARD8 underwent IL-1β secretion and cell death in response to both VbP and HIV-1 infection in a dox-dependent manner (Figure 5B and C)
evidence: The manuscript presents data showing responses in dox-treated complemented cells (Figure 5B and C).

claim: CARD8 KO THP-1 cells complemented with WT CARD8 undergo IL-1β secretion and cell death in response to HIV-1 infection in a dox-dependent manner.
source: We found that CARD8 KO THP-1 cells complemented with WT CARD8 underwent IL-1β secretion and cell death in response to both VbP and HIV-1 infection in a dox-dependent manner (Figure 5B and C)
evidence: The manuscript presents data showing responses in dox-treated complemented cells (Figure 5B and C).

claim: HIV-1 infection induces IL-1β secretion and cell death only in CARD8 KO THP-1 cells that were complemented with WT human CARD8, but not CARD8 mutants that are resistant to HIV-1PR cleavage.
source: In contrast, infection with both VSV-g pseudotyped (Figure 5B and C) and replication competent (Figure 5E and F) HIV-1LAI induced IL-1β secretion and cell death only in CARD8 KO THP-1 cells that were complemented with WT human CARD8, but not CARD8 mutants that are resistant to HIV-1PR cleavage.
evidence: The manuscript presents data comparing responses in cells complemented with WT versus mutant CARD8 (Figures 5B, C, E, F).

claim: CARD8 KO THP-1 cells complemented with chimpanzee CARD8 restore responsiveness to VbP but not to HIV-1LAI infection.
source: We also found that CARD8 KO THP-1 cells complemented with chimpanzee CARD8 restored responsiveness to VbP but not to HIV-1LAI infection
evidence: The manuscript presents data showing responses to VbP but not HIV-1 in cells complemented with chimpanzee CARD8 (Figure 5D-F).

claim: Chimpanzee CARD8 L60F is cleaved by HIV-1PR and SIVcpzPR.
source: whereas chimpanzee CARD8 L60F (i.e. chimpanzee CARD8 with the phenylalanine at residue 60 as in human CARD8) is cleaved by HIV-1PR and SIVcpzPR (Figure 5—figure supplement 1)
evidence: The manuscript presents immunoblot data showing cleavage of chimpanzee CARD8 L60F (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).

claim: Chimpanzee CARD8 L60F can functionally complement human CARD8 responses to HIV-1 infection.
source: and can functionally complement human CARD8 responses to HIV-1 infection (Figure 5D–F).
evidence: The manuscript presents data showing IL-1β secretion and cell death in cells complemented with chimpanzee CARD8 L60F after HIV-1 infection (Figures 5D-F).

claim: Human CARD8 detects the enzymatic activity of HIVPR by encoding a motif that functions as a HIVPR substrate.
source: Thus, human CARD8 detects the enzymatic activity of HIVPR by encoding a motif that functions as a HIVPR substrate, permitting a human-specific CARD8 inflammasome response to HIV-1 infection.
evidence: The manuscript shows that the F59-F60 motif is required for HIV-1PR cleavage and subsequent inflammasome activation (Figures 1, 5).

claim: The F59-F60 motif permits a human-specific CARD8 inflammasome response to HIV-1 infection.
source: Thus, human CARD8 detects the enzymatic activity of HIVPR by encoding a motif that functions as a HIVPR substrate, permitting a human-specific CARD8 inflammasome response to HIV-1 infection.
evidence: The manuscript shows that only human CARD8 with F60 responds to HIV-1 infection, while other primate CARD8 variants do not (Figures 1, 2, 5).

claim: Inflammasomes are cytosolic innate immune complexes that assemble upon detection of diverse pathogen-associated cues.
source: Inflammasomes are cytosolic innate immune complexes that assemble upon detection of diverse pathogen-associated cues and play a critical role in host defense and inflammatory pathogenesis.
evidence: This is a general statement about inflammasomes supported by established scientific knowledge.

claim: Inflammasomes play a critical role in host defense and inflammatory pathogenesis.
source: Inflammasomes are cytosolic innate immune complexes that assemble upon detection of diverse pathogen-associated cues and play a critical role in host defense and inflammatory pathogenesis.
evidence: This is a general statement about inflammasomes supported by established scientific knowledge.

claim: CARD8 consists of a disordered N-terminus, a function-to-find domain (FIIND), and a caspase activation and recruitment domain (CARD).
source: The inflammasome-forming sensor caspase recruitment domain-containing protein 8 (CARD8) consists of a disordered N-terminus, a function-to-find domain (FIIND), and a caspase activation and recruitment domain (CARD) (Taabazuing et al., 2020).
evidence: The manuscript cites Taabazuing et al., 2020 for the structure of CARD8.

claim: The FIIND is comprised of ZU5 and UPA subdomains.
source: The FIIND, comprised of ZU5 and UPA subdomains, undergoes self-cleavage resulting in two non-covalently associated fragments (D'Osualdo et al., 2011; Taabazuing et al., 2020).
evidence: The manuscript cites D'Osualdo et al., 2011 and Taabazuing et al., 2020 for FIIND structure.

claim: The FIIND undergoes self-cleavage resulting in two non-covalently associated fragments.
source: The FIIND, comprised of ZU5 and UPA subdomains, undergoes self-cleavage resulting in two non-covalently associated fragments (D'Osualdo et al., 2011; Taabazuing et al., 2020).
evidence: The manuscript cites D'Osualdo et al., 2011 and Taabazuing et al., 2020 for FIIND self-cleavage.

claim: Proteasome-dependent degradation of the N-terminus leads to the release and assembly of the C-terminal UPA-CARD.
source: Proteasome-dependent degradation of the N-terminus leads to the release and assembly of the C-terminal UPA-CARD, serving as a platform for the recruitment and activation of caspase-1 (CASP1).
evidence: This describes the established mechanism of CARD8 activation.

claim: The C-terminal UPA-CARD serves as a platform for the recruitment and activation of caspase-1 (CASP1).
source: Proteasome-dependent degradation of the N-terminus leads to the release and assembly of the C-terminal UPA-CARD, serving as a platform for the recruitment and activation of caspase-1 (CASP1).
evidence: This describes the established mechanism of CARD8 activation.

claim: Activated CASP1 initiates pyroptosis.
source: Activated CASP1 initiates a lytic, programmed cell death called pyroptosis and the release of pro-inflammatory cytokines including interleukin (IL)-1β and IL-18 (Broz and Dixit, 2016; Fink and Cookson, 2005).
evidence: The manuscript cites Broz and Dixit, 2016 and Fink and Cookson, 2005 for CASP1 function.

claim: Activated CASP1 initiates the release of pro-inflammatory cytokines including IL-1β and IL-18.
source: Activated CASP1 initiates a lytic, programmed cell death called pyroptosis and the release of pro-inflammatory cytokines including interleukin (IL)-1β and IL-18 (Broz and Dixit, 2016; Fink and Cookson, 2005).
evidence: The manuscript cites Broz and Dixit, 2016 and Fink and Cookson, 2005 for CASP1 function.

claim: DPP8/9 form an inhibitory complex with CARD8 to prevent aberrant release of the UPA-CARD.
source: To prevent aberrant release of the UPA-CARD, the dipeptidyl peptidases 8 and 9 (DPP8/9) form an inhibitory complex with CARD8 (Sharif et al., 2021).
evidence: The manuscript cites Sharif et al., 2021 for DPP8/9 function.

claim: Direct inhibition of DPP8/9 by Val-boroPro causes CARD8 inflammasome activation.
source: For example, disruptions to protein homeostasis, including direct (e.g. Val-boroPro) and indirect (e.g. CQ31) inhibition of DPP8/9, cause CARD8 inflammasome activation (Johnson et al., 2020; Johnson et al., 2018; Rao et al., 2022).
evidence: The manuscript cites Johnson et al., 2020; Johnson et al., 2018; Rao et al., 2022 for DPP8/9 inhibition effects.

claim: Indirect inhibition of DPP8/9 by CQ31 causes CARD8 inflammasome activation.
source: For example, disruptions to protein homeostasis, including direct (e.g. Val-boroPro) and indirect (e.g. CQ31) inhibition of DPP8/9, cause CARD8 inflammasome activation (Johnson et al., 2020; Johnson et al., 2018; Rao et al., 2022).
evidence: The manuscript cites Johnson et al., 2020; Johnson et al., 2018; Rao et al., 2022 for DPP8/9 inhibition effects.

claim: Treatment of HIV-1 latently infected cells with certain NNRTIs including efavirenz enforces cytosolic dimerization of HIV-1PR and results in CARD8 inflammasome activation.
source: For example, treatment of HIV-1 latently infected cells with certain nonnucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors (NNRTIs), including efavirenz (Wang et al., 2021) or doravirine-like analogs including the pyrimidines Pyr01 (Balibar et al., 2023), enforce the cytosolic dimerization of the HIV-1PR and results in CARD8 inflammasome activation in primary CD4+ T cells and humanized mouse models (Clark et al., 2022).
evidence: The manuscript cites Wang et al., 2021; Balibar et al., 2023; Clark et al., 2022 for NNRTI effects on CARD8.

claim: HIV-1PR cleavage of the N-terminus of CARD8 causes proteasome-dependent degradation of the CARD8 N-terminal fragment.
source: HIV-1PR cleavage of the N-terminus of CARD8 causes proteasome-dependent degradation of the CARD8 N-terminal fragment (Wang et al., 2021).
evidence: The manuscript cites Wang et al., 2021 for the mechanism of CARD8 activation by HIV-1PR.

claim: Functional degradation of CARD8 N-terminus liberates the UPA-CARD fragment for inflammasome assembly and activation.
source: This 'functional degradation' liberates the UPA-CARD fragment for inflammasome assembly and activation, analogous to viral protease sensing by the inflammasome-forming sensor NLRP1 (Robinson et al., 2020; Sandstrom et al., 2019; Tsu et al., 2021a; Tsu et al., 2021b; Planès et al., 2022)
evidence: The manuscript cites multiple papers on NLRP1 mechanism and draws analogy to CARD8.

claim: The N-terminus of CARD8 functions as a molecular 'tripwire' to sense and respond to the enzymatic activity of HIV-1PR and other viral proteases.
source: in which the N-terminus of CARD8 functions as a molecular 'tripwire' to sense and respond to the enzymatic activity of HIV-1PR and other viral proteases (Castro and Daugherty, 2023; Nadkarni et al., 2022; Tsu et al., 2023).
evidence: The manuscript cites Castro and Daugherty, 2023; Nadkarni et al., 2022; Tsu et al., 2023 for the tripwire model.

claim: VbP specifically activates the CARD8 inflammasome in THP-1 cells.
source: As a positive control for inflammasome activity, uninfected cells were also treated with VbP, which specifically activates the CARD8 inflammasome in THP-1 cells (Johnson et al., 2020).
evidence: The manuscript cites Johnson et al., 2020 and uses VbP as a positive control throughout the study.

claim: CARD8 is a bona fide innate immune sensor of viral infection via sensing viral protease activity.
source: These results, along with other recent findings (Nadkarni et al., 2022; Tsu et al., 2023), demonstrate that CARD8 is a bone fide innate immune sensor of viral infection via sensing viral protease activity
evidence: The manuscript presents data on CARD8 sensing of HIV-1 and cites other studies showing CARD8 sensing of other viruses.

claim: Some positive-sense RNA viruses that do not package their viral proteases are sensed following de novo synthesized viral protease.
